description: Implement CAN message authentication (e.g., MAC-based) so ECUs reject unsigned messages.
Require cryptographically signed firmware images; reject any OTA package that fails signature verification.
Enforce Bluetooth pairing with mutual authentication and disable legacy pairing modes.
Require security access (seed-key exchange) before allowing any diagnostic session beyond default level.
Use short-lived, rotating authentication tokens instead of static credentials for backend communication.
Add timestamps and nonces to diagnostic commands so replayed messages are automatically rejected.
Implement rate limiting and traffic filtering on the Gateway ECU to resist flooding.
Encrypt all telemetry data in transit using TLS between TCU and backend server.
Sandbox Bluetooth command handling and validate all inputs from paired devices before execution.
Enforce anti-rollback counters so firmware can never be downgraded below the last approved version.
Encrypt sensitive CAN payloads or segment critical ECUs onto a separate, access-controlled CAN segment.
Apply strict backend access controls, monitoring, and multi-factor authentication for administrative access.
